newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop sharply as IMF hopes evaporate.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop sharply as IMF hopes evaporate.

text.p: Thai stocks dropped sharply in the morning session as investors sold equities following Thailand''s decision not to seek IMF or Japanese assistance for the troubled Thai economy, brokers said.
The SET index dipped 16.25 points, or 2.48 percet to 640.03 by 0343 GMT. The SET 50 lost 1.58 points or 3.18 percent to 48.10 in trade worth 1.33 billion baht.
Investors were also selling on the disappointment and ahead of a long weekend as Thailand's situation remains fluid at the moment, traders said. Monday is a religious holiday.

"Investors especially local ones might want cash to spend on the weekend. Some foreign investors also don't want to hold large positions ahead of the long weekend," said one trader at a foreign brokerage.

Stocks of large finance firms set to lead consolidation in the sector were most active. Some foreign brokers, after avoiding the sector for months, have recently upgraded recommendations on these firms, traders said.
Nava Finance and Securities Plc added 1.25 baht to 24.50, Krungthai Thanakit Plc gained 0.25 to 38.75, and after a heady recent run Phatra Thanakit was off two to 51.50 by 0406 GMT.
In the broader market most key sectors were down as Thailand's economic fundamentals remain weak and the short term outlook appears gloomy, analysts said.
